newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Flavored coffees seen dominating specialty market.
newsitem.headline: Flavored coffees seen dominating specialty market.

text.p: Flavored coffees, long the fastest growing segment of the U.S. specialty coffee market, should hold a 30 percent share of the market by 1999, a top industry official said.

Ted Lingle, head of Specialty Coffee Association of America, detailed the near-term outlook for the market in a paper drawn up for distribution at a meeting in this industrial hub in northwest Colombia marking the 70th anniversary of the powerful National Coffee Growers' Federation.
"By 1999, we expect 25 percent of the specialty coffee market will be straight (unblended) coffees," the paper said.
"Fifteen percent will be blends, 30 percent will be flavored, 15 percent will be decafs, 10 percent will be dark roasts, and five percent will be organically grown," the paper said.

Calling variety a key to success in selling specialty coffee, it said such coffees should be thought of as "a mix of different product categories ... a mix well suited to filling hundreds of thousands of small niche markets, because of all the combinations and permutations available to retailers."
